milestone.title: mp autopilot orchestrator verifier — independent state-reads + role-boundary violation detection

intent.outcome: Before the orchestrator accepts any lane's 'done' notification, it independently verifies state via `mp show milestone`, `reviews.json`, and `activity.json` — and detects seven named role-boundary violations (e.g., runner called `mp reviews pass`, reviewer modified code, notify arrived before the lane was started). Violations surface as typed events on the raul autopilot tab and trigger topology-aware remediation.

problem.description: Lessons 3 (M201 cycle 1 fabricated lifecycle claim) and 4 (M203 runner self-completed via `mp reviews pass`) from the project log both stem from the orchestrator trusting the lane's report. The fix is independent state-reads (three sources, not one) and seven named violation detectors. Permission policies at the harness layer were considered and rejected per the simplification conversation — the orchestrator's verifier is the safety net, catching violations after the fact with enough specificity that remediation can be targeted (reject + resend in 3-pane; reject + escalate in 2-pane and 1-pane).

in_scope: `crates/mp/src/autopilot/verifier.rs` exports a `Verifier` struct that runs after each lane notification. It cross-references the lane's claimed state against three sources: `mp show milestone <id> --fields lifecycle,execution_status,spec_status`; the latest verdict in `reviews.json` for that milestone; the last three activity.json entries filtered by milestone subject.

Seven typed violation detectors, each returns an `Option<Violation>`: (1) Runner called `mp reviews pass`; (2) Runner called `mp reviews claim` or `mp reviews finding add`; (3) Runner modified `master-plan/` directly; (4) Reviewer modified code (`git diff crates/..` attributable to reviewer pane ID); (5) Reviewer called `mp reviews pass` before orchestrator prompt; (6) Notify arrived before the lane was started; (7) Orchestrator committed code attributable to its own pane ID.

`Violation` enum: `RunnerReviewViolation`, `RunnerClaimViolation`, `RunnerPlanEditViolation`, `ReviewerCodeEditViolation`, `ReviewerPrematurePassViolation`, `PreStartNotificationViolation`, `OrchestratorCodeEditViolation`. Each carries the evidence (activity event id, git log SHA, diff hunk).

Topology-aware remediation hook (C3 owns the policy decision; the verifier exposes a `recommend_remediation(violation, topology) -> Remediation` that C3 consults): 3-pane → `Resend(corrective_message)`; 2-pane → `EscalateToUser(violation)`; 1-pane → `EscalateToUser(violation)` (no independence to recover).
out_of_scope: The cycle-flow sequencing and decision matrix — that's C3; C2 only exposes detectors.
The lane-notification wire format — that's C1.
Per-AC evidence restoration enforcement (lesson 2 from the log) — separate small track item; C2 doesn't address it.
Harness-side permission policies — out per the simplification decision.

acceptance_criteria.description: The verifier cross-checks milestone state, latest review verdict, and session event-log entries after a durable event cursor; mismatches and missing revisions are typed errors. It does not rely on an arbitrary last-three activity tail.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test verifier_state_cross_check --no-fail-fast exit 0 (7/7 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Each role-boundary detector is exercised with attributable session fixtures. Detection uses M207 actor tokens and dispatch-bounded repository snapshots; conditions that cannot be attributed are reported as UnknownActor and block automatic acceptance rather than being guessed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test verifier_seven_violations --no-fail-fast exit 0 (18/18 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: `recommend_remediation` returns `Resend` for any violation under 3-pane, `EscalateToUser` under 2-pane or 1-pane.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test verifier_topology_remediation --no-fail-fast exit 0 (5/5 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Regression test for M201 cycle 1: a fabricated `lifecycle=executed` notification with no matching activity.json event and a milestone at `lifecycle=approved` is rejected by the verifier as a typed mismatch.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test verifier_m201_cycle1_regression --no-fail-fast exit 0 (3/3 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Documentation: `docs/mp/autopilot-verifier.md` describes (a) the `mp reviews pass` writing pattern (writes to milestone JSON + reviews.json; does NOT add an activity.json event by default), so future agents don't look for a `review-pass` event in activity.json as proof of completion; (b) the M200 recovery lesson (review-pass lost to activity.json truncation; verifier cross-checks three sources to catch it); (c) the multi-source verification convention (milestone JSON + reviews.json + activity.json).
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test autopilot_verifier_docs --no-fail-fast exit 0 (9/9 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Every autopilot mutation carries session id, role, actor token, dispatch id, and sequence number. Review pass attribution is read from the session event log plus reviews.json; missing or mismatched actor identity blocks automatic completion.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test verifier_actor_attribution --no-fail-fast exit 0 (9/9 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Before accepting runner completion, the verifier requires every step done and every AC evidence value to contain the exact command, exit code, and observed pass count. Generic summaries and evidence overwritten after completion are rejected; the canonical criterion state is re-read after completion.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test verifier_evidence_contract --no-fail-fast exit 0 (15/15 pass)

acceptance_criteria.description: Verification commands use a structured command-list representation. Parentheses in nextest filters are preserved as argv; shell control operators such as `&&`, `;`, and newlines are either represented as separate commands or rejected with an actionable typed error, never silently skipped.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p mp --test verifier_command_list --no-fail-fast exit 0 (9/9 pass)

design_decisions.choice: Each detector is a small typed function (e.g., `fn detect_runner_review_violation(events: &[ActivityEntry], pane_id: &str) -> Option<RunnerReviewViolation>`); the Verifier composes them.
design_decisions.rationale: Pure functions are testable in isolation; new detectors add without changing existing ones.

design_decisions.choice: Violations carry structured evidence (activity event id, git log SHA, diff hunk) so remediation can act on specifics, not just 'something violated'.
design_decisions.rationale: Forensic without being heavy; matches the M190 sequencer's evidence pattern.

design_decisions.choice: `recommend_remediation` lives in C2 (verifier), but the policy enum (`Resend` / `EscalateToUser`) is shared with C3 (cycle flow).
design_decisions.rationale: C2 owns the surface; C3 owns the cycle-flow consumption.

design_decisions.choice: Role violations are accepted only with session-scoped actor provenance or dispatch-bounded repository evidence; uncertain attribution becomes a blocking UnknownActor result.
design_decisions.rationale: Activity and git history do not inherently identify a herdr pane. Guessing would create false accusations and still miss the M203 violation.
